description: The top of the ladder: Glowmere over 1.21 square kilometres at glowmere-medium's per-square-metre density and species proportions. 1100 m is where the ladder stops being a ladder rather than where the machine stops coping -- past it the visible-instance count falls again (3,111 at 1100 m against 1,564 at 1200 m) because the composer's viewpoint lands on different ground, and Grass_Common_Short has already reached the composer's 120,000-instance ceiling for a foreground layer, which it crosses between 950 m and 1000 m, so the ground here is 13% thinner underfoot than glowmere-dense's. Both are measured in docs/renderer-2-benchmark-world.md. This rung hurts: read it as one fixed heavy scene to compare against itself, not as a point to interpolate through.

certification.what: The top of the ladder, and heavier than the authored Glowmere. The other rung §6 says to judge a regression on.
certification.declares: The counters below are what this rung submits at the resolution, tier and camera named here, and they are checked exactly by tools/certify.py. They can be: a composition is a pure function of (recipe, library, seed) and the culling decision a pure function of that plus the camera and the resolution, so an unequal count is a real change every time and carries no noise floor to argue about. The frame times are measured in the same run and are deliberately NOT declared -- a millisecond is a property of a session (01-audit-and-baseline.md §3.1), and a declared one would be a cross-session comparison with the other session hidden inside a constant.
